messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: `DEDICATED_TENANT_LATENCY` triggered for tenant=AtlasCorp. Priority P1. Links: https://pd.example/INC12345. Reason: sustained p95 latency > 2s and 429 throttles from reserved pool.

omar (oncall): paging — I'm up, acked the PD alert. I see spike in request queue depth for AtlasCorp on reserved-pool-7.

marta (sre): @omar can you paste the top logs (tail) from the scheduler? want to see autoscale decisions.

omar (oncall): sure, tail from 1912345600 -> 1912345660:
```
2026-03-14T20:01:12Z scheduler: tenant=AtlasCorp pool=reserved-pool-7 queued=120 in_flight=32 autoscale_decision=NO_SCALE reason=below_cpu_threshold
2026-03-14T20:01:20Z router: tenant=AtlasCorp resp_status=429 rate_limit=reserved_capacity_exhausted
2026-03-14T20:01:35Z serving: kv_cache_miss tenant=AtlasCorp hit=0 miss=85
2026-03-14T20:01:40Z scheduler: tenant=AtlasCorp queued=135 in_flight=28
```

marta (sre): hmm looks like autoscaler didn't kick despite queue growth. could be metric bug or policy mis-eval.

chen (platform): I'm on it — checking autoscale-policy configs for reserved-pool-7. @marta any chance we recently changed `max_burst` or paused scale?

marta (sre): Not that I saw. @omar can you run `rctl get autoscale reserved-pool-7 --tenant AtlasCorp` and share output?

omar (oncall): running now...
```
rctl> policy: conservative_queue
rctl> min_replicas=2 max_replicas=10 cooldown=300s scale_metric=cpu_threshold
rctl> burst_override=null
```

marta (sre): scale_metric=cpu_threshold explains why queue didn't trigger — cpu is low because requests are mostly short, but queue is building due to KV-cache misses. Need to trigger manual scale + increase burst.

pd-ops: PD incident note: escalation to Platform team requested. @chen please respond in PD.

chen (platform): acknowledging on PD. I'm going to bump reserved capacity for AtlasCorp temporarily. Executing: `rctl scale reserved-pool-7 --tenant AtlasCorp --replicas 6`

omar (oncall): command output: `Scaling request accepted, new_replicas=6 (pending)`. Router is showing 50% fewer 429s so far.

atlas-sre (customer): seeing improved throughput but some requests still 5-6s. Any ETA?

sam (customer-success): FYI I notified AtlasCorp that we're investigating and temporarily boosting capacity. They asked if this will be disruptive — said no if we keep it short.

marta (sre): next mitigation: warm KV cache for top prefixes to reduce per-request work. @omar can you run `cache-prefill` job for AtlasCorp top-50 prefixes?

omar (oncall): kicked off prefill job: job_id=pf-191234. Logs show prefill started at 1912345850.

incident-bot: Update: PagerDuty INC12345 acknowledged by omar (oncall) at 1912345702.

chen (platform): prefill job results: 34/50 keys warmed in 90s; backend error on a few keys (403 from internal auth) — looks like one of AtlasCorp's keys rotated unexpectedly. Notifying customer.

atlas-sre (customer): confirmed we rotated a service key during maintenance window, sorry — returning new key to you now.

omar (oncall): once key replaced, we saw cache hit rate jump to 78% and p95 latency dropped under 800ms. 429s nearly eliminated.

marta (sre): good. mitigation summary: 1) manual scale to 6 replicas 2) cache prefill + key fix 3) temporary routing fallback to hosted when reserved capacity saturated (enabled as safety).

pd-ops: notating timeline in PD: alerted at 1912345678, acked 1912345702, mitigation actions at 1912345725-1912345900, customer key rotation completed 1912345935, recovery observed 1912345980.

chen (platform): Follow-up action items: - add queue_rejection metric to autoscaler policy for reserved pools - add a fast-path scale trigger on sustained queue growth - add alert to customer key rotation during active traffic (detect stale tokens).

marta (sre): Agreed. I'll open incidents/ postmortem template and assign owners. Short follow-up: estimate impact — ~15% of AtlasCorp traffic saw 429s or >=2s tail latency for ~22 minutes. No other tenants impacted.

sam (customer-success): I'll coordinate a post-incident update to AtlasCorp and ask them for any logs of failed calls.

omar (oncall): handing off to marta for postmortem. I'm clear in 10m.

marta (sre): I'll run the blameless postmortem. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler policy used cpu threshold which didn't capture backlog from KV cache exhaustion; combined with rotated service key causing cache misses. Root cause likely config + out-of-band key rotation.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC12345 resolved at 1912346005 (status: resolved).

marta (sre): closing thread but leaving notes: ticket INF-2147 created for autoscaler changes, assigned to @chen. Ticket INF-2148 for detection of key rotation impacts assigned to @sam + @atlas-sre.

atlas-sre (customer): appreciate the quick response — thanks @omar @marta.

omar (oncall): thanks all. marking as resolved on Slack. :white_check_mark:
